{{Quote|I'm Commander Trinnolt Makken, Imperial Navy, retired. I'm your government-appointed observer.|Trinnolt Makken, to Tahiri Veila|<ref name="Outcast" />}}
'''Trinnolt Makken''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] born prior to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. At one point in his life, he lost his left [[Limb/Legends|hand]] and received a [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic]] replacement. Makken served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]] in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] but retired from service by [[43 ABY]], when he was appointed by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] to be the [[Jedi supervisor]] of former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tahiri Veila]]. The job of a [[Supervisor/Legends|supervisor]] was to shadow [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] on their missions to help keep the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Order]] in line. However, as Veila was no longer a Jedi, she resisted and took the matter to court. In the [[The Galactic Federation of Free Alliances versus Tahiri Veila|ensuing trial]], the Galactic Alliance [[Court of Justice]], led by [[Chief Justice]] [[Uved Pledesin]], ruled with Veila. Makken was later put in charge of the [[Galactic Alliance Department of Justice|Department of Justice's]] investigation into the [[Skirmish in the Operations Hangar|death]] of interim Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Kenth Hamner]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Commander, I'm not a Jedi.''"<br />"''It applies to Sith, too, when they can be identified.''"<br />"''I'm not a Sith, either.''"<br />"''Regardless, your name is on the document.''"<br />"''Not Jedi. Not Sith. Do you fly? Thrusters from metal arm, thrusters from nostrils? Then don't come back until you do, because you may find yourself dropping two hundred stories out a viewport.|Tahiri Veila and Trinnolt Makken|<ref name="Outcast" />}}
Trinnolt Makken was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] who was born at least by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Makken lost his left [[Limb/Legends|hand]] at some point around 32 BBY,<ref name="birth" /> and he received a [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic]] replacement. He served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]] in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], and he retired from service by the time following the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. In [[43 ABY]], he was appointed by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] to be the [[Jedi supervisor]] of former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Tahiri Veila]]. Jedi supervisors were tasked with following a Jedi on all of their missions to help keep the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in line. Makken went to Veila's home in [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Residential district]], where he told Veila that he was to be her supervisor. Veila laughed and claimed that since she was no longer a Jedi, she did not require a supervisor, to which Makken replied that the law applied to [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] as well. Veila, however, was no longer a Sith, either; she had become a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of her [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], [[Darth Caedus]], during the [[Battle of Uroro Station]].<ref name="Outcast" />

Veila finally convinced Makken to leave her by threatening to throw him out her [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]]. The matter was later taken to court in ''[[The Galactic Federation of Free Alliances versus Tahiri Veila]]'', with the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] lawyer [[Nawara Ven]] helping to defend Veila. The [[Court of Justice]], led by [[Lorrdian/Legends|Lorrdian]] [[Chief Justice]] [[Uved Pledesin]], ruled with Veila, stating that a being's possession of skills did not necessarily constitute the need for a supervisor.<ref name="Outcast" /> Later, in [[44 ABY]], Commander Makken was put in charge of the [[Galactic Alliance Department of Justice|Department of Justice's]] investigation into the recent [[Skirmish in the Operations Hangar|death]] of interim Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Kenth Hamner]]. He was among the many governmental representatives to attend [[Funeral of Kenth Hamner|Hamner's funeral]].<ref name="Con" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|This is not a joke. I have legal identification.|Trinnolt Makken, to Tahiri Veila|<ref name="Outcast" />}}
Trinnolt Makken was brief and abrupt when dealing with others. He often dispensed with pleasantries, preferring to get straight to business. When talking with Veila, Makken showed that he was also arrogant and rather grim, responding humorlessly to her cynical and often sardonic remarks.<ref name="Outcast" /> Commander Makken was described as aristocratic in appearance, with pale skin,<ref name="Con" /> [[Color/Legends|white]] hair, and blue eyes,<ref name="Outcast" /> and his left hand was prosthetic.<ref name="Con" /> Makken made no attempt to hide the fact that his hand was prosthetic, preferring instead to keep the replacement visibly mechanic.<ref name="Outcast" />

==Behind the scenes==
Trinnolt Makken made his first appearance as a minor character in the first [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] novel, ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]'', written by [[Aaron Allston]]. He later appeared in Allston's ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'', the seventh novel in the series.
